title: Git Security
description: Secure Git workflows by preventing secret leaks, verifying signatures, and protecting against repository tampering.

data.text: Git was designed for collaboration, not secrecy. By default, every commit, branch, and tag is visible to anyone with repository access. Advanced Git security means controlling who can write, what can enter history, and how you verify that commits are authentic.

The most common security incident in Git is accidentally committing a password, API key, or certificate. Once committed, that secret is in the history forever unless you rewrite it. Prevention is far cheaper than remediation.

items: Use a `.gitignore` to exclude files that contain secrets.
Run pre-commit hooks with tools like `gitleaks` or `git-secrets` to block commits containing sensitive patterns.
Scan repository history periodically with automated secret-scanning tools.

data.title: Block secrets with gitleaks
data.code:
# Install gitleaks
git clone https://github.com/gitleaks/gitleaks.git

# Run against the repository
gitleaks detect --source=. --verbose

data.text: GPG-signed commits and tags prove that a change came from a specific person's key. Platforms like GitHub and GitLab display a Verified badge next to signed commits, which helps consumers trust release artifacts.

data.title: Sign a commit and tag
data.code:
git config --global user.signingkey <your-key-id>

# Sign a commit
git commit -S -m "feat: add secure payment flow"

# Sign a tag
git tag -s v1.2.3 -m "Release 1.2.3"

data.text: If a secret is already in history, assume it is compromised. Rotate the credential immediately, then rewrite history to remove it using `git filter-repo` or BFG Repo-Cleaner. Force-push the cleaned history and notify every clone to re-clone or reset.

data.title: Remove a secret from history with BFG
data.code:
# Download BFG
java -jar bfg.jar --replace-text passwords.txt repo.git

# Clean up and repack
git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now --aggressive

git push --force

data.title: Revoke before you rewrite
data.text: Do not wait for the history rewrite to finish before rotating the exposed credential. An attacker can use the secret in seconds. Rotate first, clean history second.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: Prevent secret commits with pre-commit hooks and secret-scanning tools.
Sign commits and tags to prove authorship and build trust.
If a secret leaks, rotate it immediately, then rewrite history.
Use tools like BFG or `git filter-repo` for efficient history cleaning.
